transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-11
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Ben (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Luis (Redwood CSM), Priya (Springwell Head of ML), Aaron (CTO), Sofia (Procurement), Daniel (Platform)

-- Auto-summary generated (optional) --
Maya: quick tour of console focusing on per-route dashboards, cost breakdown by token and model, and how to set up route tagging for billing allocation.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ben: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we're the Redwood team, we'll do a 30-ish minute console walkthrough and then leave time for questions. Priya, Aaron, you good with that agenda?
[00:12] Priya: yep that works for us thanks Ben, just curious to see the cost split per-route — that's been the big unknown.
[00:18] Aaron: and curious about VPC/private deployment options and how that changes the analytics, yes.
[00:24] Ben: perfect we'll tee that up. Maya over to you.
[00:30] Maya: awesome, hey all — so first slide is the usage analytics home, this is what teams typically see day to day, total token volume, model mix, average latency, error rates, and cost over time. note, some fields are auto-aggregated, if you see odd values that can be from transcription or mapping (eg model name might show as redwood-1 instead of exact model).
[01:02] Maya: the top left shows overall consumption, you can apply time filters, group by route, by user, or by model; right now i'm going to filter to the patient-support route to see specifics.
[01:18] Maya: here you can see token-level cost columns, this is our estimate based on model used, quantization profile, and infra. it's not a billing invoice but a close approximation for allocation purposes.
[01:33] Priya: when you say token-level cost is that like per-token billing or an internal metric?
[01:38] Maya: good question — it's an internal unit economics view; we compute per-token cost including GPU cycles, batching efficiency, and cache hits. you can export it and map to your chargeback system.
[01:51] Aaron: does that take into account batch size variance or prefix caching?
[01:56] Maya: yes we model batching and KV cache hit rate; if you enable prefix caching for say FAQ routes your per-token cost can drop significantly, you'll see that reflected in the dashboard as reduced effective tokens.
[02:10] Daniel: small note — our security team will want to know what PII shows up in these console exports.
[02:16] Maya: exports are metadata-only by default, actual transcript/text is redacted unless you enable it; we also have hooks to strip PII or mask via regex rules before storage.
[02:28] Sofia: and the retention policy? procurement asks frequently.
[02:31] Ben: we have configurable retention; hosted defaults to 90 days on the console, enterprise dedicated/private customers can opt for longer retention or send logs to their S3/Kinesis.
[02:44] Priya: okay good, show us per-route dashboards.
[02:47] Maya: yep, switching to the per-route view — each route has its own dashboard: volume over time, model used, latency percentiles, error breakdown, and cost-split. here we have patient-support, triage, and summarization routes.
[03:03] Maya: the neat bit is tagging — if you tag routes with product lines or teams, cost allocation becomes automatic. i'm going to drill into triage route.
[03:14] [03:15] Maya: triage is interesting, lots of short prompt calls, we show a balloon plot of latency vs tokens. most of their traffic is sub-300 tokens which is great for batching.
[03:25] Priya: is there a way to see which model variants are falling back? we had a canary and sometimes it falls back to a bigger model.
[03:32] Maya: yes, we show rollout history per-route — you can see percentage allocation to primary/canary and fallback events. the console also logs why fallback happened (eg capacity, model error, timeout).
[03:44] Aaron: and can we set route-level SLOs? we need triage under 250ms p95.
[03:50] Maya: route-level SLOs are supported — you can set latency SLOs and build automated routing policies: prefer low-latency pool but fall back to cheaper pool if cost budget hit.
[04:01] Daniel: that fallback, does it preserve response format? we rely on structured output.
[04:06] Maya: yes, format-preserving fallbacks map model outputs through the same response schema; function calling and structured outputs are supported across variants. occasionally the SE said ''model sometimes uses a different tokenization'' — small caveat but we do validation checks.
[04:21] Priya: let's look at cost breakdown for the last 30 days.
[04:25] Maya: switching to cost breakdown, top row is total cost by route, second row is cost by model family, and we have token bucket breakdown for inference vs embeddings vs reranking.
[04:36] Maya: here's an example: triage is 42% of cost but only 28% of traffic — that's because it hits the larger model during peak windows, you can see the model timeline.
[04:49] Ben: quick interjection — sometimes token costing has small variances due to quantization differences and kernel selection, so we show a confidence interval on cost estimates.
[04:59] Sofia: procurement — from a contracting standpoint, how deterministic are these numbers for budgeting?
[05:04] Ben: for reserved/dedicated capacity we can give solid unit economics and committed throughput numbers; hosted is usage-based so monthly can vary, but you can set alerts and caps. with Dedicated you get better predictability.
[05:18] Aaron: can we run a pilot on Dedicated or do we start on Hosted?
[05:22] Maya: most pilots start hosted with a reserved baseline for burst; we can move to dedicated once throughput and SLOs are defined. for Springwell we can propose a short hosted benchmark first, then recommend Dedicated if predictable throughput needed.
[05:36] Priya: benchmark — what does the template need from us?
[05:39] Maya: sample traffic profile (payload sizes, tokens distribution), 1 week of synthetic or replay data, target p95/p99 SLOs, success criteria (latency and cost per 1M tokens), and sample routes to measure. i'll share the template.
[05:53] Daniel: we'll need a postman collection or simple harness, yes please.
[05:57] Maya: included.
[06:00] [06:02] Maya: back to dashboards, admins can add tags, set budgets per-route and get alerts when spend approaches threshold, also you can send detailed chargeback CSVs to your billing system.
[06:14] Priya: is the chargeback CSV per-request or aggregated?
[06:17] Maya: both options — per-request row-level CSV up to 30 days, and aggregated monthly rollups for cost allocation.
[06:25] Sofia: on security — SOC2 and encryption, KMS integrations, audit logs?
[06:29] Ben: we are SOC2 Type II, provide customer audit artifact pack on request. for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM and full audit log streaming to your S3 or SIEM.
[06:42] Daniel: how are SSO and RBAC handled? we need fine-grained roles for analysts vs infra.
[06:46] Ben: we support SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC with route-level permissions. you can scope access so analysts see dashboards but not raw payloads.
[06:58] Priya: any known gaps for healthcare PHI compliance?
[07:02] Ben: we support HIPAA adjacency setups for Private deployment — e.g., on-prem or in a VPC with customer-side logging and KMS. hosted can be used but we'd need a BAA and specific controls; we should bring legal into that thread.
[07:18] Sofia: good note — we'll need the security pack for procurement.
[07:21] Ben: yes we'll include SOC2 report, BAA template, and a short security FAQ.
[07:25] Maya: moving on, here's an example of anomaly detection in the console — eg sudden spike in model substitution or a steep latency increase — those generate alerts and suggested mitigations.
[07:38] Priya: that alerting can we hook into PagerDuty?
[07:41] Maya: yes webhook, PagerDuty, Slack, and custom integrations.
[07:46] Aaron: about model variants — do you have quantization recommendations? we saw docs about q4 vs fp16 tradeoffs.
[07:53] Maya: Redwood Optimize suggests quantization profiles per-route based on latency vs quality tradeoffs; the console surfaces recommended profiles and expected cost savings, you can apply them on a canary.
[08:05] Daniel: will quantization affect hallucination or quality for our summarization route?
[08:10] Maya: typically small effect, we recommend running quality evals with your prompt set; Optimize ties regression alerts to eval sets so you won't miss a quality drop.
[08:20] Priya: can you show an example of eval tied to a route?
[08:22] Maya: sure — here's a route where we run daily evals against 200 golden prompts and flag regression if F1 accuracy drops below threshold; you can see trends in the same UI.
[08:36] [08:40] Maya: switching back to cost — i want to highlight per-route allocation rules: you can tag a route to split cost across multiple teams if needed, e.g., 70/30.
[08:50] Sofia: procurement ask — what about committed spend discounts?
[08:53] Ben: reserved capacity and committed spend discounts are available for Dedicated, for hosted we offer volume tiers. we'll put pricing bands in the spreadsheet.
[09:04] Priya: latency numbers — can you show a p95 chart?
[09:07] Maya: here's p50/p95/p99, note the p95 spikes during batch windows; you can correlate with batch size and concurrency.
[09:16] Aaron: can we instrument custom traces into our app to correlate user-visible latency to model latency?
[09:21] Maya: yes tracing hooks and distributed tracing tags; route id passes through, and you can add correlation IDs to track user-to-model latency.
[09:30] Daniel: small transcription blip — earlier you said KV cache, the security doc sometimes calls it K V cache in text, minor but make sure docs match.
[09:37] Maya: yes thanks, we'll ensure consistent naming.
[09:40] [09:45] Priya: on data residency — we have multiple regions, can you pin routes to a region?
[09:49] Maya: you can route by policy: prefer region A for EU patients, region B for US, and enforce pinning for sensitive routes (Private supports stricter controls).
[10:00] Priya: that's critical for us.
[10:02] Ben: quick question from procurement — can logs be purged on demand?
[10:06] Ben (cont): yes on Dedicated/Private, and hosted with a request/contracted retention.
[10:12] Sofia: ok perfect.
[10:14] Maya: heading to the final slide — recommended pilot: 2-week hosted benchmark, triage + patient-support routes, our team runs the benchmark and you provide sample traffic. deliverables: latency/cost report, suggested routing and quantization.
[10:30] Priya: timeline ok for us, is 2 weeks enough?
[10:33] Maya: for initial numbers yes, for long-term tail behaviour we'd extend, but two weeks gives good signal.
[10:41] Aaron: what resources do you need from us to start?
[10:44] Maya: sample traffic, target SLOs, list of top 5 routes, contact for networking (for VPC) if needed.
[10:52] Daniel: we'll compile that and aim to send by 02-16.
[10:56] Ben: great. any final questions?
[11:00] Priya: just on invoicing — can we get estimates per route in the pricing doc?
[11:04] Ben: yes we'll include sample cost models per route.
[11:07] Sofia: and security pack please.
[11:09] Ben: will do.
[11:12] Maya: i'll attach the benchmark template and postman collection in the follow-up email.
[11:18] Aaron: thanks everyone, looks good.
[11:20] Ben: thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials and schedule the pilot.

Recap / Next steps (automated):
